text:
This looks like mid-2010: the unemployment rate is 9.7%, the fed funds rate is 0.15%, the VIX is 34, and equities fell sharply over three months, which fits the May-June 2010 flash crash and the Euro crisis. The 10-year yield at 2.97% points to June 2010, when it was about 3.2%, or possibly later.

Several figures need checking against that window:
- Industrial production growth was about +8% YoY in mid-2010, which fits.
- Core CPI at 0.97% fits mid-2010 (about 0.9% in June or July).
- Headline CPI at 1.96% fits May or June 2010, when it was about 2.0%.
- The VIX closed at about 34.5 at the end of June 2010, which matches 34.13 fairly well.
- The 10-year yield ended June 2010 at about 2.97%, which matches.
- US large-cap equity fell about 5.2% in June 2010, but the table shows -3.6% for the month. The 3-month figure of -11.4% would better fit the period from the end of March to the end of June, when the S&P was down about 11.9%.
- Gold's 12-month return of +33% also fits.

The snapshot is most likely June 2010.
